commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][CPU] Enable C++ causal_conv1d GDN path and float32 SSM cache on non-AMX AVX-512BF16 CPUs
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

CPU GDN attention (Qwen3.5) selects its causal-conv1d implementation via `torch.cpu._is_amx_tile_supported()`: AMX CPUs (Intel GNR) use the C++ kernels (`causal_conv1d_fwd_cpu` / `causal_conv1d_update_cpu`), everything else falls back to `causal_conv1d_fn_cpu` / `causal_conv1d_update_torch`, a pure-PyTorch per-sequence loop.

The C++ conv kernels (`csrc/cpu/sgl-kernels/conv.cpp`) do not use AMX tiles but `is_amx` gate blocks it from running on non-AMX platforms that support AVX-512BF16.

The float32 SSM state(currently gated by `is_amx` is required for entire CPU GDN path, not just AMX

This PR fixes this gating logic.


## Test plan

Extended `tests/kernels/mamba/cpu/test_cpu_gdn_ops.py` (all gated on `_is_avx512_bf16_supported()`, so they run on non-AMX CPUs too).

Expected Result: 105 passed, 0 skipped on both Intel GNR and AMD Turin.

```bash
python -m pytest tests/kernels/mamba/cpu/test_cpu_gdn_ops.py -v
```

Qwen-3.5 workload run before and after the patch on both Intel GNR and AMD EPYC Turin

```
  VLLM_CPU_OMP_THREADS_BIND=0-63 
  VLLM_CPU_KVCACHE_SPACE=40 
  vllm bench throughput \
    --model Qwen/Qwen3.5-9B \
    --trust-remote-code \
    --dataset-name random \
    --input-len 1024 \
    --output-len 1024 \
    --num-prompts 128 \
    --max-num-seqs 32 \
    --dtype bfloat16 
```
    
 
Lmeval

```
VLLM_CPU_OMP_THREADS_BIND=0-63 \
VLLM_CPU_KVCACHE_SPACE=40 \
lm_eval \
  --model vllm \
  --model_args "pretrained=Qwen/Qwen3.5-9B,dtype=bfloat16,trust_remote_code=True,max_model_len=4096" \
  --tasks gsm8k \
  --num_fewshot 5 \
  --batch_size auto 
```


## Test result


Python GDN test Result: 105 passed, 0 skipped on both Intel GNR and AMD Turin.


Workload Qwen3.5-9B, BF16, ISL/OSL 1024/1024, 64-core instance (median of 3 runs)

Intel GNR is unchanged (it takes the identical path both ways, so no regression). 
AMD EPYC Turin gains about 9-10% on this memory-bound, decode-heavy shape,
which is the hardest case for a conv speedup to show up.

## Correctness

`lm_eval` gsm8k, 5-shot, full set (n=1319), Qwen3.5-9B BF16, before vs after:

| Platform | Metric | Baseline | After |
|----------|--------|---------:|------:|
| Intel GNR (AMX) | exact_match | identical | identical |
| AMD Turin (Zen5) | flexible-extract | 0.8696 +/- 0.0093 | 0.8749 +/- 0.0091 |
| AMD Turin (Zen5) | strict-match | 0.8734 +/- 0.0092 | 0.8779 +/- 0.0090 |

GNR is bit-identical (same code path both ways). On Turin, before/after differ by less than one standard error, so there is no accuracy regression. The C++ conv accumulates in fp32 and is numerically no less accurate than the torch fallback(both round to bf16 at store), which the unit tests also assert against an fp32 oracle.


## Duplicate Check

Searched open PRs/issues for GDN / causal_conv1d / Zen / AVX-512BF16 CPU conv work; found none addressing the non-AMX conv fallback.

This PR Fixes #49640

commits.pr_title: [ROCm] Add UE8M0 scale packing for Triton silu_mul_quant
commits.pr_body:
Adds UE8M0 (int32 packed) scale output support to the Triton `_silu_mul_fp8_quant_deep_gemm` fallback kernel on ROCm. Depends on:
- #37833

The Triton kernel computes float32 scales, then packs them into int32 UE8M0 format by extracting the float32 exponent bits (bits 30:23).

This is effectively dead code on ROCm today (UE8M0 requires DeepGEMM which is CUDA-only), but ensures feature parity and removes a test skip.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][CI] Extended Fused MoE and FP8 MoE test support
commits.pr_body:
This PR makes the fused MoE layer test matrix usable on ROCm/MI355 by fixing the real ModelOpt FP8/FP4 failures it exposes and by making distributed subcase failures visible to pytest.

Key changes:

- Propagate fused MoE distributed subcase failures back to the parent pytest process instead of allowing child-rank failures to print as failed subcases while the parent test reports `PASSED`.
- Allow `modelopt_fp4` MoE test configs on gfx950 alongside the existing SM100 path, where native or emulated NVFP4 execution is available.
- Use the existing NVFP4 reference quantization path to create packed FP4 test weights on ROCm, since `ops.scaled_fp4_quant` is not available there.
- Keep NVFP4 emulation lookup tensors on the same device as the packed FP4 input during dequantization.
- Preserve reduced ModelOpt FP8 tensor-wise MoE activation scales as backend-neutral 0-D tensors, reshaping them only at the Triton launch boundary so FlashInfer retains its scalar ABI while Triton receives a loadable pointer.
- Gate the experimental MoRI fused MoE layer matrix behind `VLLM_TEST_ENABLE_MORI_MOE_LAYER=1`; when enabled, the test sets the AITER fused MoE env requirements and disables AITER shared expert fusion.
- Enable the modular OAI Triton MoE test on CUDA-like platforms and pad MXFP4 test weights/inputs to the CDNA4 scale-layout alignment on ROCm while slicing outputs back to the original test shape.

AI assistance: OpenAI Codex was used to analyze the CI and review feedback and to prepare the changes.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] compressed-tensors: restore int8 grouped WNA16 MoE support
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Restores the fix from #47154, which was lost in #44570.

#47154 dropped the `group_size == -1` assert from the int8 branch of
`CompressedTensorsWNA16MarlinMoEMethod` so that checkpoints with group-quantized int8
experts could load. #44570 then merged that class into
`CompressedTensorsWNA16MoEMethod`, deleting the fixed file and keeping the other
class's version of the branch, which still carried the assert.

Net effect: any compressed-tensors checkpoint whose MoE experts are not all quantized
to the same width fails to load again, on 0.27.0 onwards.

| tag | `assert self.group_size == -1` |
|---|---|
| v0.25.1 | absent |
| v0.26.0 | absent |
| v0.27.0 | present |
| v0.27.1 | present |
| main | present |

## Test Plan

Repro is `poolside/Laguna-XS-2.1-INT4`, the checkpoint #47154 was written for. Its
experts are mixed: int4 g128 on layers 1-30, int8 g128 on layers 31-39 (we are testing with A4500 GPUs).

vllm serve poolside/Laguna-XS-2.1-INT4 --tensor-parallel-size 2 --max-model-len 131072

Layers 1-30 build, layer 31 hits `assert 128 == -1`. No download needed to see it — the
constructor alone is enough:

```python
from compressed_tensors.quantization import (
    QuantizationArgs, QuantizationStrategy, QuantizationType)
from vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.compressed_tensors.compressed_tensors_moe.compressed_tensors_moe_wna16 import (  # noqa: E501
    CompressedTensorsWNA16MoEMethod)

CompressedTensorsWNA16MoEMethod(
    QuantizationArgs(num_bits=8, type=QuantizationType.INT,
                     strategy=QuantizationStrategy.GROUP, symmetric=True,
                     dynamic=False, group_size=128),
    None,
    moe_config,   # any FusedMoEConfig
)
```
Test Result

Before, on 0.27.0 (2x RTX A4500, TP=2). This is the whole output — the assert has no
message and no worker traceback surfaces, even at VLLM_LOGGING_LEVEL=DEBUG:

```
INFO  [gpu_model_runner.py:5308] Starting to load model poolside/Laguna-XS-2.1-INT4...
INFO  [compressed_tensors_moe.py:132] Using CompressedTensorsWNA16MoEMethod
INFO  [int_wna16.py:297] Using 'MARLIN' WNA16 MoE backend.
ERROR [multiproc_executor.py:912] AssertionError
ERROR [core.py:1349] Exception: WorkerProc initialization failed due to an exception in a background process.
```

The MARLIN/WNA16 lines are info_once from layer 1 and are misleading: the assert
runs during layer construction, before backend selection and before any weights are
read. No flag works around it — --moe-backend, --enable-expert-parallel,
--enforce-eager and the VLLM_*_MOE_* / VLLM_MARLIN_* env vars are all evaluated
later.

After, with the line removed: the assert no longer fires and construction proceeds to
backend selection.

commits.pr_title: [Core] Skip broadcasting mm tensor data to workers for prefix-cache-covered items
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Fixes #52040.

## Background: why this gap exists and who it affects

The EngineCore->TP-worker broadcast was designed when request inputs were token IDs (kilobytes), so shipping them unconditionally was both correct and free. Multimodal grafted large tensors onto the same path, but for the classic workload (a fresh image per chat request) the workers genuinely need every tensor, so unconditional shipping remained necessary. What changed recently is multimodal **prefix caching**: there now exists a state -- "this item's tokens are fully KV-covered" -- in which the shipped tensors are provably never consumed, and the broadcast becomes pure per-request CPU overhead.

The workload that exposes this is the emerging **streaming / agentic multimodal** pattern: an assistant that re-sends a rolling window of frames every turn (a live camera or video feed with a position-stable layout, so prefix caching covers all history images). For that pattern the cost is linear in window size on every request -- ~19 ms x 25 images = ~0.5 s of EngineCore CPU per turn in our deployment -- while the tensors themselves (fixed-size fp32 pixel patches, ~15.5 MB per image at our processor settings) are re-serialized into the ring for workers that will never touch them. As this workload class grows (streaming VLM assistants, video agents, multi-turn visual memory), the benefit of skipping compounds: it turns fully-cached multimodal TTFT from linear-in-images into flat.

When a multimodal item's placeholder span lies entirely within the prefix-cache-covered region, no encoder run can ever be scheduled for it — yet its processed tensors are still serialized into the EngineCore→TP-worker broadcast, per unique item, on every request. For workloads that re-send a rolling window of images (fully prefix-cached), this makes TTFT grow linearly with attached image count: we measured ~19 ms per unique image at TP=4 with 15.5 MB `pixel_values` per image (evidence, flamegraphs, and a duplicate-image control experiment in #52040).

This PR extends the existing `MultiModalFeatureSpec.data = None` convention (already used to skip API-server→EngineCore IPC on processor-cache hits) one hop further, to the worker broadcast:

- `NewRequestData.from_request` strips `data` from items whose span is fully inside `num_computed_tokens` (new helper `strip_covered_mm_data`, same file).
- The scheduler-side `Request` keeps the full features, so nothing is lost engine-side.
- **Preemption safety**: requests resumed from preemption re-ship their features via a new `CachedRequestData.resumed_mm_features` field, re-stripped against the post-eviction computed-token count — so items uncovered by eviction regain their data before their encoder runs are scheduled. The worker applies these in its resumed-request branch.
- The worker's encoder-input batching already tolerates `data is None` (existing `continue` in `_batch_mm_inputs_from_scheduler`), and the v2-runner path folds resumed requests through `from_request`, so it re-evaluates the strip condition naturally.

For the rolling-window workload this removes ~25 tensor broadcasts per request; the fully-cached TTFT floor becomes flat in image count (~4 ms/image of parse+hash remains, which is intrinsic to content addressing).

## Test Plan

- Added unit tests for `strip_covered_mm_data` in `tests/v1/core/test_output.py`: fully-covered and boundary items stripped, uncovered kept, already-None preserved, input list not mutated, zero-computed no-op.
- Logic additionally verified standalone; I was not able to run the full test suite locally (no GPU dev box) — relying on CI here, and happy to iterate.
- Live-workload validation available on our deployment (TP=4, Gemma-4-31B vision, 26-image rolling window): expected effect is the fully-cached floor dropping from ~630 ms to near the 2-image floor. Can report numbers once a build with this change is deployable.

## Test Result

Unit tests pass locally at the logic level; awaiting CI for the full suite.

## Notes for reviewers

- The strip is deliberately conservative: it only removes data for items that *cannot* have encoder runs scheduled given current `num_computed_tokens` at ship time; every path that changes that quantity downward (preemption/resume) re-ships.
- An alternative, larger design would move mm tensor transport to `scheduled_encoder_inputs` time entirely (ship exactly when an encoder run is scheduled). Happy to pursue that instead if preferred — this PR takes the minimal-diff route.

commits.pr_title: [Kernel] SM120: stop routing misaligned-M blockwise FP8 GEMMs to the small-M swapAB config
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

The SM120 blockwise FP8 GEMM dispatch routes **every** call with `M % 4 != 0` to the
swapAB config (TILE_N=32), which was added in #38325 as a small-M/decode optimization:

```cpp
bool swap_ab = (M <= 64) || (M % 4 != 0);
```

Under V1 chunked prefill, mixed prefill+decode batches routinely make M misaligned at
prefill scale (M ~ 8k). In an Nsight Systems capture of Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 (a dense 27B
hybrid linear-attention model: 64 layers, 3:1 gated-delta-net to full attention, FP8
e4m3 blockwise) serving 8192/1024-token requests at concurrency 32 on an NVIDIA RTX PRO
6000 Blackwell Server Edition (SM120), 82% of prefill-scale blockwise GEMM
instances (14400/17523) went through the swapAB path, where they averaged 4.84 ms vs
3.10 ms on the default 128x128x128 config. The misroute roughly doubled prefill GEMM
time end-to-end.

Force-routing both paths over a dense M x N x alignment matrix (M = 48..8192 including
M%4 in {0,1,2}, N in {5120, 15360, 34816}, K = 5120) shows:

- swapAB only wins at M <= ~80 (its intended decode regime);
- from M ~ 96-128 up, the non-swap configs win everywhere, by 1.3x-2.0x at prefill scale;
- outputs are **bit-identical** between the swapAB and non-swap paths at every measured
  misaligned point, so the `M % 4 != 0` clause has no correctness role on SM120.

The fix restricts swapAB to its design regime:

```cpp
bool swap_ab = (M <= 64);
```

Note: `scaled_mm_blockwise_sm90_fp8_dispatch.cuh` (`(a.size(0) % 4) != 0`) and
`scaled_mm_blockwise_sm100_fp8_dispatch.cuh` (`(m < 16) || (m % 4 != 0)`) carry the same
misaligned-M clause. They are untouched here because the measurements above are
SM120-only; the same recheck may be worthwhile on those targets.

## Test Plan

- Microbenchmark driving `torch.ops._C.cutlass_scaled_mm` across an M x N x alignment
  matrix with both kernel paths force-routed (temporary env-var instrumentation, not
  included in this PR), comparing per-path latency and bitwise outputs.
- End-to-end serving benchmark before/after: 8192-token prompts, 1024-token outputs,
  concurrency 32, NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition, Qwen3.8-27B-FP8.

## Test Result

Microbenchmark (N=34816, K=5120):

| M | before (ms) | after (ms) |
|---|---|---|
| 64 | 0.13 | 0.13 (unchanged, still swapAB) |
| 8192 (M%4==0) | 3.86 | 3.89 (unchanged) |
| 8193 | 7.89 | 4.12 |
| 8225 | 7.64 | 3.92 |

Outputs at M=8193/8225 are bit-identical before and after.

End-to-end (concurrency 32, 8K/1K):

| metric | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| output throughput | 424.6 tok/s | 499.8 tok/s (+17.7%) |
| mean TTFT | 9660 ms | 6872 ms |
| mean TPOT | 65.9 ms | 57.3 ms |

The patched build reaches parity with an SGLang baseline of the same model, shapes, and
hardware (501.2 tok/s), closing what was previously an ~18% gap that traced back to this
misroute.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][LoRA] Guard None group members in expand_packed_lora (partial LoRA on Qwen3.5/3.6 GatedDeltaNet)
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Fix a crash when loading a LoRA adapter that targets only some members of a GatedDeltaNet
packed projection group on Qwen3.5/Qwen3.6 (e.g. `in_proj_qkv` without `in_proj_z`).
`expand_packed_lora` dereferenced `b_i.shape[0]` on a `None` group member, raising
`AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'shape'`.

This is a regression introduced by #37912, which unified the GDN input projections into a
fused packed layer and added `expand_packed_lora` — but the new helper didn't carry over the
`None`-tolerance that its sibling `slice_lora_b` and the `set_lora` stacking loop already
have. Partial groups worked in v0.20.0 (which built the projections as separate modules under
LoRA via `create_in_proj_qkvz`).

Fixes #47639

## Fix

Make `expand_packed_lora` skip `None` group members, emitting `None` placeholders for the
slice(s) they cover so subsequent groups stay aligned, leaving those slices at base weights.
This restores partial-group support inside the current fused architecture without reverting
the #37912 split.

`expand_packed_lora` is only reached for the `in_proj_qkvz` group (2 members → 4 slices);
every other packed group has `len(lora_b) == n_slices` and takes the normal,
already-`None`-tolerant path. In `in_proj_qkvz` the multi-slice member (`in_proj_qkv`) leads
and the optional member (`in_proj_z`) trails, so a `None` member covers exactly the remaining
slices (documented in a code comment).

## Test Plan

End-to-end on 1x H200, vLLM 0.24.0, torch 2.11.0+cu130, with a real Qwen3.6-27B LoRA adapter
targeting `q_proj,k_proj,v_proj,in_proj_qkv` (i.e. `in_proj_z` absent):

- **Before the fix:** `add_lora` fails during adapter activation with
  `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'shape'` in `expand_packed_lora`
  (server exits with `ValueError: Call to add_lora method failed: ...`).
- **After the fix:** the same `vllm serve ... --enable-lora --lora-modules my_lora=<adapter>`
  starts and applies the adapter successfully.

## Notes

- AI assistance was used to author this change; I have reviewed every changed line, understand
  the fix, and ran the tests above.
- Not a duplicate: checked open PRs/issues for `expand_packed_lora` / partial LoRA on Qwen3.5
  GDN before filing — see #47639.

@Isotr0py
@jeejeelee

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Return all choices from /inference/v1/generate when n > 1
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

closes #52398

`serve_tokens` sets `sampling_params.output_kind` only for streaming requests, so non-streaming ones keep the `SamplingParams` default, `CUMULATIVE`. With `n > 1`, `serve_tokens_full_generator` keeps only the last streamed `RequestOutput` and reads `final_res.outputs`, which under `CUMULATIVE` holds just the sequences updated in that step,
the other completions are silently dropped. No error is raised; the response is simply short.

`CompletionRequest.to_sampling_params` already uses `FINAL_ONLY` when not streaming, so this makes the
token-in-token-out path match it.

## Test Plan

10 non-streaming requests per `n` (2, 4, 8) against `vllm serve Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B` on an H100, before and after the patch, counting the choices returned by `/inference/v1/generate`. Same check with multimodal input (`/v1/chat/completions/render` → `token_ids` + `features`, Qwen2.5-VL-3B). Streaming, `logprobs`, `prompt_logprobs` and `n=1` re-checked after the patch. Adds a regression test asserting the response carries indices `0..n-1`.

## Test Result

Before:

```
n=2 -> {1: 6, 2: 4}
n=4 -> {2: 5, 3: 3, 4: 2}
n=8 -> {5: 2, 7: 5, 3: 1, 6: 2}
multimodal, n=4 -> 3 choices on 6/6 runs
```

After:

```
n=2 -> {2: 10}
n=4 -> {4: 10}
n=8 -> {8: 10}
multimodal, n=4 -> 4 choices on 6/6 runs
```

`n=1`, streaming, `logprobs` and `prompt_logprobs` behave as before. The measurements were taken on v0.27.1 with this
patch applied to the installed package; the added test follows the existing fixtures in `tests/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/test_serving_tokens.py` and will get its first full run in CI.

commits.pr_title: [CI] Fix docs build
commits.pr_body: Fixes the Read the Docs build, which fails with `TypeError: metaclass conflict` importing `vllm.benchmarks.serve`: docs build without torch, so `nn.Module` was a `MagicMock` instance and `class Attention(nn.Module, AttentionLayerBase)` clashed with `ABCMeta` (newly fatal because `model_loader/reload/layerwise.py` now pulls the attention layer into the benchmark import chain). This mocks `torch.nn.Module` as a real class, mocks `torch` itself with that `nn` attached (since `import torch.nn as nn` goes through `getattr(torch, "nn")`), caches the torch-availability check so that extra mock does not disable the others, and lets the mock `register` accept kwargs. No open PR covers this (`gh pr list --search "generate_argparse in:title,body"`). Tested by reproducing the traceback on `main` in a torch-free Python 3.12 venv from `requirements/docs.txt`, then running `python -m mkdocs build` with the fix: succeeds in 442s with populated CLI and engine-args pages; `pre-commit` passes. No evals: docs tooling only, no effect on model output or serving. AI assistance (Claude Code) was used; I reviewed every line and ran the tests above.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Restore model info caching for package backends
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

This PR only restores ModelInfo caching for package backends. It does not attempt to resolve the overall startup-time gap between the Transformers backend and native vLLM. Other startup costs discussed in #50128 are outside this PR's scope.

Related to #50128.

After #26906 changed the Transformers backend from `transformers.py` to a package, the ModelInfo cache continued looking for the removed file. `module_hash` therefore remained `None`, skipping cache reads and writes.

This PR falls back to `importlib.util.find_spec()` when the flat file is absent, allowing package backends to use the existing cache logic.

```bash
uvx ruff check \
  vllm/model_executor/models/registry.py \
  tests/models/test_registry.py

python -m pytest -q --confcutdir=tests/models \
  tests/models/test_registry.py -k lazy_modelinfo
```

Start the server twice in separate processes with the same cache directory:

```bash
VLLM_CACHE_ROOT=/tmp/vllm-modelinfo-cache \
VLLM_LOGGING_LEVEL=DEBUG \
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B \
  --model-impl transformers \
  --enforce-eager
```

For each run, measure from process start to the first successful `/health` response. Stop the first server before starting the second.

commits.pr_title: fix: reject string schemas that mix pattern/format with length bounds
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

`has_xgrammar_unsupported_json_features` misses a class of silently-wrong input: a string schema that mixes a generative constraint (`pattern` or `format`) with `minLength`/`maxLength`. xgrammar compiles the pattern/format side and drops the length bounds from the grammar entirely, so the request is accepted and the model can return strings that violate the bound with no error anywhere. Reject the combination at validation time so the caller gets a clean 400 instead of quietly wrong output.

## Verification

Evidence that the bounds really are dropped, on the current xgrammar (compiled EBNF via `xgr.Grammar.from_json_schema`):

- `{"type":"string","pattern":"^a+$","maxLength":2}` produces `root_1 ::= (("a" root_1) | ("a"))`, identical to the same schema without `maxLength`. No length cap in the grammar.
- `{"type":"string","format":"email","maxLength":10}` and the same schema without the bound compile to byte-identical EBNF.
- `{"type":"string","maxLength":2}` with no pattern does lower to `{0, 2}`, so the bounds only go missing once a generative constraint is present.

Change coverage: the checker now flags `pattern + minLength/maxLength` and `format + minLength/maxLength`, nested objects and array items included. 13 cases verified against the exact shipped function (the four new rejections, plus pattern-only, format-only, length-only, and the pre-existing checks still intact). The pytest fixtures in `tests/v1/structured_output/test_utils.py` mirror those cases for CI; the full structured-output suite needs a GPU-less box with torch installed, so the rest is left to CI.

Note: this replaces my older #45599, which went stale when the structured-output code was restructured (the file it touched no longer exists). The guidance backend is unchanged here; its handling of the same combination is a separate question I have not verified.

## Test Plan

- [x] `has_xgrammar_unsupported_json_features` rejects pattern/format + length combos, including nested positions (object property, array items)
- [x] Pattern-only, format-only, and length-only string schemas still pass
- [x] New fixture cases added to `tests/v1/structured_output/test_utils.py`
- [ ] Full structured-output test suite (needs torch-capable CI runners)

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Redact api_key in startup logs and compile cache factors
commits.pr_body:
## What

The API server startup log prints all non-default arguments verbatim:

```
INFO ... [api_utils.py:273] non-default args: {'model_tag': 'org/model', 'api_key': '***', ...}
```

So --api-key / VLLM_API_KEY lands in plain text in container and host
logs. Anyone with log read access (docker logs, host filesystem, log
shippers) recovers the API key from a single startup line.

A second leak: compile_factors() starts from every registered VLLM_*
env var, and the raw factor dict is persisted on disk in
cache_key_factors.json (compiled-artifacts cache metadata). Since
VLLM_API_KEY was not excluded, the key was also written in plaintext to
that file — and it additionally invalidated the compile cache on every key
rotation.

This PR:
- redacts the api_key value to *** in the startup log, keeping the
  field name so operators can still tell a key was configured
- excludes VLLM_API_KEY from compile_factors() so it is neither hashed
  into the cache key nor persisted in cache_key_factors.json

Only the logging path and the factor list are touched;
get_non_default_args() and the --args-json handoff to the Rust frontend
are unchanged (the frontend stores keys as hashes).

## Why this is not duplicating an existing PR

Searched open PRs/issues for api_key redact, api_key mask, `api_key
leak` in title/body: no open PR or issue addresses this log line.

```

ruff format --check vllm/entrypoints/serve/utils/api_utils.py  # already formatted
pytest tests/entrypoints/serve/utils/test_api_utils.py -v
14 passed (11 pre-existing + 3 new redaction tests)
```

This PR was developed with AI assistance (Claude). The change is small
and self-contained; please flag if the approach looks off.

free real estate for anyone reading logs. I've fixed mine by rotating;

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Run the serve arg checks for `vllm launch` too
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

`vllm launch render` silently skips every one of the pre-load serve argument checks, so an invalid flag combination is accepted at the CLI and only fails (or misbehaves) later.

`vllm/entrypoints/cli/main.py` registers subcommands with `dest="subparser"` and then calls `cmds[args.subparser].validate(args)`. `LaunchSubcommand.validate` calls `validate_parsed_serve_args(args)`, and `LaunchSubcommandBase.add_cli_args` builds the component parser with `make_arg_parser`, so `vllm launch render` genuinely accepts the full serve flag set. But the first line of the validator is:

```python
if hasattr(args, "subparser") and args.subparser != "serve":
    return
```

For `vllm launch render` `args.subparser` is `"launch"`, so the function returns before doing anything. Everything it guards is skipped:

- `validate_chat_template(args.chat_template)`
- `--enable-auto-tool-choice` requires `--tool-call-parser`
- `--enable-log-outputs` requires `--enable-log-requests`
- `--enable-per-request-metrics` conflicts with `--disable-log-stats`
- `validate_multi_port_external_lb_args` for `--data-parallel-multi-port-external-lb`

The `hasattr` half of the guard is still needed: `vllm/entrypoints/openai/api_server.py`'s `__main__` block parses with `make_arg_parser` and no subparser at all, and must be validated. Only the `!= "serve"` half is wrong now that `launch` exists.

This changes the CLI contract in the direction the code already intended, catching bad arguments at parse time instead of letting them through. `vllm serve` behaviour is unchanged, and a subcommand that does not build its parser from `make_arg_parser` is still skipped.

## Not a duplicate

No open or merged PR touches `validate_parsed_serve_args`'s subparser guard, and no open issue reports `vllm launch` skipping serve validation. The `launch` subcommand and its `render` component are recent, and the guard predates them, which is how the gap opened.

## Test Plan

Two tests added to `tests/entrypoints/openai/test_cli_args.py`, next to the existing serve-validation tests:

- `test_launch_render_validates_serve_args` builds the parser the way `vllm/entrypoints/cli/main.py` and `LaunchSubcommandBase.add_cli_args` do (`dest="subparser"`, nested `launch render` component built from `make_arg_parser`), asserts `args.subparser == "launch"`, and asserts `--enable-auto-tool-choice` with no `--tool-call-parser` raises `TypeError`.
- `test_subcommand_without_serve_args_skips_validation` pins the remaining purpose of the guard: a subcommand that does not carry serve args is still skipped and must not raise.

```
pytest tests/entrypoints/openai/test_cli_args.py -k "launch_render or without_serve_args"
```

## Test Result

I do not have a GPU or a vLLM build in my environment, so the pytest run above is left to CI. What I did run locally:

1. A standalone `argparse` harness that reproduces the exact wiring (root parser with `dest="subparser"`, a `serve` subparser and a nested `launch render` subparser, both built by the same `make_arg_parser` stub) plus the validator's guard and its first check:

```
serve --enable-auto-tool-choice           subparser=serve   before='TypeError: --enable-auto-tool-choice requires --tool-call-parser'  after='TypeError: ...'
launch render --enable-auto-tool-choice   subparser=launch  before='SKIPPED'                                                          after='TypeError: ...'
```

So `launch render` is skipped before the change and validated after, while `serve` is unaffected.

2. `ruff check` and `ruff format --diff` on both changed files. `ruff format` reports both already formatted, and `ruff check` reports exactly the same four pre-existing findings before and after the change (`PLR0402`, `RUF010`, `PIE807` in `cli_args.py`, `I001` in `test_cli_args.py`), none on a line this PR touches.

This is a CLI argument-validation change only. It does not touch sampling, kernels, model execution or output, so there are no accuracy or serving benchmark numbers to report.

commits.pr_title: [Attention][MLA] FlashMLA sparse: DCP on the fp8_ds_mla mixed-batch path + MTP
commits.pr_body:
DCP support for the `FLASHMLA_SPARSE` backend on the `fp8_ds_mla` KV path, including MTP spec decode under full cudagraphs. `fp8_ds_mla` is what the backend selector picks on Hopper for DSA models with small per-rank head counts (GLM-5.2 / DeepSeek-V3.2 at TP4/DCP4), and this path previously refused DCP outright.

Earlier revisions stacked on #46076 and carried the sparse-indexer DCP machinery (global top-k merge, `--dcp-sparse-indexer-mode`); all of that has since landed in main via #46076 and its follow-ups, so the PR is now backend-side only: +234/−34 across `flashmla_sparse.py`, `flashmla.py` and one test file. (#45426 was our earlier standalone version with its own indexer; this supersedes it and reuses the upstream merge machinery instead.)

## Changes

`flashmla_sparse.py`:
- Opt the backend into the shared DCP decode merge (`can_return_lse_for_decode`): the fp8 mixed-batch kernel now returns decode LSE, sliced together with the head padding and reshaped to the `(tokens, heads)` layout the reducer consumes.
- Under DCP the indexer emits global token ids: keep this rank's shard and convert to local `fp8_ds_mla` slots via `triton_filter_and_convert_dcp_index` with `compact_valid_to_front=False` — the scattered `-1`s stay in place and the fp8 kernel masks them natively, skipping the per-call front-pack. Rows where this rank owns none of the selected tokens get `(0, -inf)`, the identity of the cross-rank LSE merge, so they drop out of the reduce.
- Allow varlen decode under DCP (`supports_dcp_with_varlen` when `cp_kv_cache_interleave_size == 1`): causality comes from the indexer's top-k indices, not kernel metadata. This is what makes MTP + DCP work under full cudagraphs.
- Fail-closed guards instead of silent corruption: `ag_rs` comm backend only; fp8 mixed-batch path only (the split prefill/decode path returns LSE for decode tokens only, and the bf16 sparse path is rejected under DCP); a head-envelope guard rejecting configs where local and DCP-gathered head counts pad to different fp8 decode kernel envelopes (e.g. 128 q-heads at TP8/DCP8).

`flashmla.py` (dense FlashMLA decode): flatten the kernel's `[batch, heads, seq_len]` LSE to `[tokens, heads]` for the DCP reducer — matters under spec decode, where `seq_len > 1`.

Tests: `test_fp8_dcp_head_envelope_guard` in `test_sparse_mla_backends.py`, parametrized over local head counts × DCP world sizes, both accepting and rejecting cases.

## Testing

4×H200, GLM-5.2-NVFP4, TP4/DCP4/EP + MTP, `fp8_ds_mla`, current rebase:

- `test_sparse_mla_backends.py` + `test_indexer_dcp_localize.py`: 140 passed / 0 failed (SM90).
- Full cudagraph capture clean; exact needle recovery at 198k context across all ranks.
- Warm decode 78 tok/s at batch 1, 854 aggregate at batch 32 (786k context window).
- dcp=1/2/4 byte-identical on long (>2048-tok) contexts in earlier revisions of the same merge path.

The branch has also been soaking continuously since mid-July on a production 4×H200 GLM-5.2-NVFP4 deployment (TP4/DCP4/EP + MTP) via nightly-based images carrying this PR.

Related fixes in the surrounding DCP infra that this path exposed were split out and handled separately: #48379 (fp8_ds_mla boot on main, merged), #50823 (block-table width under DCP, merged), #50883 (offload block-size scaling under DCP, open).

AI assistance (Claude) was used; every line reviewed by the submitter, tests run by the submitter.

Earlier revisions added an opt-in `--dcp-sparse-indexer-mode {exact,union}` on top of #46076's global top-k merge, motivated by a ~30% batch-1 decode regression of the exact merge vs our standalone indexer (#45426): 52.0 → 36.4 tok/s warm at batch 1, with union recovering to 43.5 and a follow-up localizer opt to 50.7. commits.pr_title: [Model] Add GraniteSWA and GraniteMoeSWA via existing Granite
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Supersedes and closes #48270

Add vLLM support for GraniteSWA and GraniteMoeSWA models, folded into the existing Granite and GraniteMoeShared implementation, as opposed to separate models as in #48270. 

- GraniteSWA: Granite with per-layer sliding-window attention and a learnable per-head attention sink. The sink is passed to Attention via the native vllm attention harness, the per-layer windowing via config.layer_types and config.sliding_window, and per-layer RoPE/NoPE via config.layer_rope_theta (0 for NoPE).
- GraniteMoeSWA: GraniteMoeShared-style MoE combined with the SWA/sink attention above (reuses GraniteSWAAttention). Optional shared experts via shared_intermediate_size (disabled by default); routed experts load through the standard FusedMoE param mapping.

Additional features (sinks, sliding window, varying RoPE) are off by default, leaving existing Granite checkpoints unaffected. Also add checkpoint remapping for handling both old- and new-style HF MoE layers. Register both [***]ForCausalLM classes in the model registry, since HF publishes these Granite variants as distinct models.

NB: transformers backend does NOT handle these models correctly. Sink tokens get dropped silently and so the model gives wrong output (see #52156).

Claude was used to assist in implementing these changes. I have reviewed, corrected, and contributed the code myself, and tested the output for correctness.

## Test Plan

Tests include offline parity checks against the adapted HF implementations, addition of SWA/MoeSWA checkpoints to the Granite tests, additional unit tests for case handling of added features and HF naming schemes, and GSM8K verification. Testing env uses CUDA 13.0, Torch 2.13.0, and Transformers 5.16.0. I have not included the parity check script(s) in this PR.

## Test Result

All unit tests pass. I have confirmed that this code produces identical output to the HF implementation at fp32 precision, and that the transformers modeling backend does not. Bfloat 16 is near-identical (one missed token prediction in a teacher-forced setting on a randomly initialized model). Parity checks include sinks on/off, RoPE varying/global, and TP on/off. GSM8K score for the 2B SWA model is within 2 points of the published HF model card (40.3 vs 42.2 for 5-shot).

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][XPU] Fix Mamba state pointer overflow
commits.pr_body:
Fixes #48059

## Purpose

XPU USM device pointers can exceed the positive signed int64 range. The Mamba
align-mode fused copy path stores state tensor and block-table `data_ptr()`
values in `torch.int64` metadata buffers before passing them to Triton kernels,
so assigning a high-bit XPU pointer directly can raise:

```text

```

This preserves the 64-bit pointer pattern by reinterpreting unsigned pointer
values as signed int64 before storing them in the existing metadata buffers. The
Triton kernel ABI stays unchanged.

commits.pr_title: [CPU] Add AMX-only high-performance MLA backend for DeepSeek V2/V3/R1
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Add `AMXMLABackend`/`AMXMLAImpl`, a high-performance MLA attention backend for
CPU, built on AMX decode/extend/bmm/qkv-proj kernels vendored under
`csrc/cpu/sgl-kernels/`. It plugs into the same `MLACommonBackend`/
`MLACommonImpl` abstraction every other concrete MLA backend uses.

This is a separate, opt-in-by-capability backend alongside the existing
reference `CPUMLABackend` (#49453): that one targets any CPU/dtype at
block_size=16 as a functional/CI reference, not performance. This backend
requires AMX (bf16 only, block_size a multiple of 32) and is preferred
automatically by the platform layer when the host supports it, falling back
to the reference backend otherwise (or when explicitly requested).

## What's included

- Vendored SGLang AMX kernels (`decode.cpp`, `extend.cpp`, `bmm.cpp`,
  `qkv_proj.cpp`) under `csrc/cpu/sgl-kernels/`, AMX-only build-gated.
- `AMXMLABackend`/`AMXMLAImpl` (`vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/amx_mla.py`):
  weight absorption for prefill via VNNI-packed `W_UK`/`W_UV` computed once at
  load time; `forward_mha` attends directly against the paged latent cache in
  one causal pass (fresh prefill + cached-prefix continuation together, no
  GPU-style decompress-then-dense-attend); `forward_mqa` reuses the existing
  generic decode-side absorption. Per-step-invariant metadata (block-table
  expansion, `req_pool_indices`, `num_kv_splits`, `query_start_loc`
  derivatives) is computed once in `AMXMLAMetadataBuilder.build`, not
  recomputed per layer.
- Platform wiring: `CpuPlatform.get_attn_backend_cls` selects `AMX_MLA` when
  `torch.cpu._is_amx_tile_supported()` and x86 (unless the reference backend
  is explicitly requested); block-size/chunked-prefill config forcing is
  scoped to exclude the AMX path, since the extend kernel handles arbitrary
  prefix length and block size natively.
- Two small, genuine bugs fixed in shared MLA code, both applicable beyond
  this backend: (1) CPU's generic `Linear` weight-packing path was freeing
  `kv_b_proj`'s raw weight before `MLAAttention.process_weights_after_loading`
  could read it to derive `W_UK`/`W_UV`; (2) `get_mla_prefill_backend()`
  unconditionally resolves the CUDA-only `FlashAttnPrefillBackend` when
  `device_capability` is `None`, which asserts at construction time on CPU —
  fixed via a minimal inert CPU prefill backend registration.
- Correctness tests (`tests/kernels/attention/test_amx_mla.py`), gated on
  `torch.cpu._is_amx_tile_supported()`, wired into the x86 CPU CI job.

## Tests

pytest -x -v -s tests/kernels/attention/test_amx_mla.py
```
10 passed (stable across repeated runs).

```

1585 passed, 990 skipped, 0 failed — no regression to the existing dense
`CPU_ATTN` backend from the shared-code changes.

Also verified directly: offline single/multi-prompt inference (coherent,
correct output on `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite`); a forced mixed
decode+prefill batch (confirmed via temporary instrumentation that
`num_decodes>0 and num_prefills>0` in the same step, output unaffected);
tensor parallelism at TP1/TP2/TP4 (correct output, no crashes, expected

commits.pr_title: [XPU] Support EC connector KV Offloading on XPU
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

PR #47423 added `ECCPUConnector` for encoder-cache (EC) offloading to host memory, but the swap path assumed CUDA/ROCm-style raw pointers and was never exercised on XPU. This PR adds XPU support so the EC connector's offload path works correctly on Intel GPUs, and extends CI coverage accordingly.

Three issues were fixed:

### 1. Descriptor pointer dtype on XPU

`swap_blocks_batch` takes `int64` pointer arrays on CUDA/ROCm but `uint64` on XPU, so `DescriptorBufferPool` now selects `_PTR_DTYPE` per platform.

### 2. Pointer assignment overflow

`ECCPUWorker.save_caches` / `start_load_caches` fill those descriptor buffers with raw addresses, and XPU USM pointers have the top bit set (value >= 2\*\*63). Torch range-checks each assigned Python int against the tensor dtype, and **the accepted encoding differs by torch version**: before 2.14 the value is always unpacked as a signed `long long`, while [pytorch#191458](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/191458) (landed as [pytorch@c9f91bd](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/commit/c9f91bddef7d6f2fffced9e9e58d3577af46d34c), released in 2.14) makes the unpacking dtype-aware.

Writing a top-bit pointer into the XPU `uint64` buffer therefore fails on *both* sides depending on how it is encoded:

| assigned value | torch 2.13 (currently pinned) | torch 2.14 |
|---|---|---|
| raw address | ❌ `ValueError: Overflow when unpacking long long` | ✅ |
| two's-complement rewrite (`addr - 2**64`) | ✅ | ❌ `OverflowError: can't convert negative int to unsigned` |

An earlier revision of this PR used the two's-complement rewrite, which crashed the engine on torch 2.14:

```
File "vllm/distributed/ec_transfer/ec_connector/cpu/worker/__init__.py", line 114, in save_caches
    src_ptrs[idx] = encode_ptr_for_dtype(src_base + start, ptr_dtype)
OverflowError: can't convert negative int to unsigned
→ vllm.v1.engine.exceptions.EngineDeadError
```

Since vLLM pins `torch==2.13.0` today but must keep working across the 2.14 bump, neither encoding is viable on its own. The descriptor tables are plain CPU tensors, so the pointer arrays are instead filled through **numpy views**, which cast against the array dtype and never go through torch's scalar unpacking — correct on both versions, and already the approach used by the KV-cache offload path (`gpu_worker.py`).

The views are created once per allocation and cached next to the tensors, and the workaround is confined to a single method so it is trivially removable later:

```python
def set_ptrs(self, idx: int, src: int, dst: int) -> None:
    # TODO(torch>=2.14): drop this indirection and assign the tensors
    # directly once the minimum supported torch is 2.14. ...
    self.src_np[idx] = src
    self.dst_np[idx] = dst
```

Only the pointer arrays need this; `sizes` holds byte counts and keeps plain torch assignment.

See [RFC #50834](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/50834) for the broader effort to unify device-pointer storage on `torch.uint64`; [this comment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/50834#issuecomment-5312646469) records the version-dependence in detail.

commits.pr_title: [Elastic EP] Reduce eager-mode reconfiguration downtime
commits.pr_body:
## Summary

This PR moves more work out of the blocking commit state to background preparation.

1. Run all preparation steps as one async worker RPC instead of returning to the DP engine core after every step.

2. Create the target EPLB communicator during preparation alongside the other target communicators, then run the post-scale-up EPLB reshuffle asynchronously.

3. During commit, switch to the prepared groups immediately, then destroy the old communication groups in the background, which can take several seconds for large groups.

4. Warm target communication groups during preparation, avoiding the much slower first collective during commit.

This solves eager-mode downtime except for kernel warmup, which will be addressed together with CUDA graph capture in a follow-up PR.

## Results

All tests used NIXL EP, async EPLB, eager execution, warm caches, and one client per DP rank.

`Preparation` is the period during which requests continue to be served unaffected. `Downtime` is the period during which new requests receive HTTP 503 and existing requests are not progressed.

### DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat, H100, DP 4 -> 8 -> 4

1 node with 8 * H100 GPUs.

| Direction | Baseline preparation | This PR preparation | Baseline downtime | This PR downtime | Downtime reduction |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Scale up | 32.208 s | 36.723 s | 6.488 s | 1.925 s | 70.3% |
| Scale down | 3.036 s | 4.897 s | 4.227 s | 1.272 s | 69.9% |

### DeepSeek-V3, GB200, DP 16 -> 24 -> 16

6 nodes, 4 GB200 GPUs per node.

| Direction | Baseline preparation | This PR preparation | Baseline downtime | This PR downtime | Downtime reduction |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Scale up | 35.855 s | 42.995 s | 13.172 s | 5.097 s | 61.3% |
| Scale down | 4.108 s | 7.768 s | 7.889 s | 3.264 s | 58.6% |

**The higher downtime in the full-size, multi-node setup comes almost entirely from the longer forward-pass warmup during commit.**

## Follow-up

With these optimizations, we consider eager-mode downtime solved. The next step is to move the max-token warmup and CUDA graph recapture into preparation. For a multi-node DeepSeek-V3 deployment, capture and warmup across the default batch sizes up to 256 take about 37 seconds. This will be addressed in a separate PR.

commits.pr_title: Revert DSv4 eager workspace reuse
commits.pr_body:
## Summary

Revert #49236 and restore allocator-backed temporary buffers in the DeepSeek V4 attention input-preparation path.

This removes the model-wide `DeepseekV4EagerScratchPool`, its output-buffer plumbing, and the out-parameter fused op added by #49236. Later changes on `main` are preserved.

## Why

The model-wide scratch pool can reuse storage across layers and CUDA streams without the caching allocator's stream/event lifetime tracking. That allows a producer to overwrite shared workspace while a previous consumer may still be using it. Reverting restores the pre-#49236 allocation lifetime behavior until safe cross-stream synchronization is implemented.

#52401 subsequently restored the wide eager region for Model Runner V1 because the narrow region corrupted V1 output. The allocation overhead remains eager on that path, so its TTFT impact is runner-dependent and has not been measured on the current tree.

## Duplicate-work check

This is not duplicating an existing revert. I checked issue #45861 and searched open PRs for references to #49236 and for DeepSeek V4 workspace/eager-scratch reuse. No open PR is dedicated to reverting #49236.

commits.pr_title: [Core] Make prefix-cache NONE_HASH deterministic by default
commits.pr_body:
## Summary

Prefix-cache block hashes chain from `NONE_HASH`. When `PYTHONHASHSEED` was unset, `NONE_HASH` was seeded with `os.urandom(32)`, so every process produced different block hashes for identical content. This forced distributed KV cache users (shared-FS/object tiers, Mooncake connector) to pin a common `PYTHONHASHSEED` on every node just to get cache hits, and made the P2P tier refuse to start without it.

This makes `NONE_HASH` derive from a fixed default seed instead, so independent instances share a prefix cache out of the box. `PYTHONHASHSEED`, if set, still overrides the default seed.

Reported by a user who found that all vLLM instances need the same `PYTHONHASHSEED` to reuse KV cache across nodes.

## Why the per-process randomness is no longer needed

The random seed dates to #12621, when prefix caching used Python's built-in `hash()` and a predictable `hash(None)` (constant on Python 3.12+) made intentional collisions feasible. The default hash algorithm is now **SHA-256**, whose collision resistance does not depend on a secret seed, and `cache_salt` is the supported mechanism for intentional cache isolation. The random seed therefore no longer adds meaningful protection while it does add operational complexity.

This also makes CBOR-based hashes reproducible by default, so the prior non-reproducibility warning is removed.

## P2P tier

The P2P tier no longer requires `PYTHONHASHSEED`: it resolves the same effective seed (`PYTHONHASHSEED` or the default) and still advertises and verifies it during the connect handshake, so mismatched peers are rejected loudly instead of silently missing.

## Docs

FS/object tiers, Mooncake connector, and P2P tier docs are updated to reflect that a shared `PYTHONHASHSEED` is now optional.

## Not a duplicate

Searched open PRs and issues for `NONE_HASH`, `PYTHONHASHSEED`, and `deterministic block hash`. The nearest hits are prefix-cache tooling/routing (#48838, #48369, #43483); none change the seed behavior.

## Tests run

- `pytest tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p/test_manager.py tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p/test_sessions.py` → **241 passed**
- `pytest tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py` → **89 passed**
- Full `pre-commit` (ruff, ruff-format, mypy, typos, SPDX, config validation) → clean

## Model evaluation

Not applicable: block content still fully determines the hash, so serving correctness (never serving another request's KV) is unchanged. This only changes the chain's starting seed.

commits.pr_title: [CI][ROCm] Prevent Git maintenance races during shallow fetches
commits.pr_body:
The ROCm test-image build in [Buildkite build 84415](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/84415/summary?jid=01a015b8-b7d5-453a-9aba-b7ea591fa5a9&tab=output#L86) failed before the Docker build with:

```text
Deepening history to reach a version tag
fatal: shallow file has changed since we read it
```

`ci-bake-rocm.sh` performs several shallow-history fetches in sequence. By default, `git fetch` may start automatic repository maintenance in a detached process. That maintenance can outlive the fetch that launched it and update `.git/shallow` while a later deepen operation is reading it, causing Git's consistency check to abort with exit status 128. The same [Buildkite step was retried on a different agent](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/84415/summary?jid=01a015c3-9b1e-4b7c-b33b-d265fe7aabe6&tab=output) and passed the history-deepening operation, image build, and `AMD image smoke OK`, confirming that the original failure was transient rather than caused by the PR's dependency change. This change:

- adds `--no-auto-maintenance` to the centralized ROCm Git fetch helper;
- applies the protection to both its timeout and no-timeout paths; and
- preserves every fetch caller's existing arguments and failure behavior.

commits.pr_title: [ROCM][CI] Attention test speedup
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Two independent problems make `tests/kernels/attention` far slower than the work it actually performs, and both are addressed here.

**1. `test_merge_attn_states.py` skips its entire matrix on ROCm without reason.**

The test gates all 2592 parametrized cases behind an "only CUDA supports the custom merge_attn_states kernel" check. That is no longer accurate: the kernel source is not CUDA-gated in the build, so it is compiled for ROCm as well, and the op is registered and produces correct results there. The same file already exercises the native kernel on ROCm through its `both_empty` case, which passes today so the wide skip contradicts a test sitting next to it.

The platform check moves from the test body to a module-level condition that accepts CUDA and ROCm. This unlocks 2592 cases of real kernel coverage on ROCm.

Because the check was evaluated inside the test body, every skipped case still paid full setup and teardown, so the group was spending minutes to decide not to test anything.

**2. Pure kernel modules pay a global cleanup after every single test.**

An autouse fixture tears down the distributed environment and empties the allocator caches after each test. The modules touched here do not build an engine and do not initialize distributed state, so there is nothing for that teardown to clean — but it still costs a garbage collection and a cache flush per test, which dominates the group's runtime.

These modules are marked with the existing `skip_global_cleanup` marker, the same mechanism already used at module level elsewhere in the test suite.

Module selection is deliberately conservative. On ROCm the global cleanup also refreshes AITER class-level state that `monkeypatch` does not restore, so every module that touches environment variables or AITER, plus one that patches platform classes, is intentionally left untouched. Nothing is given up by that: the largest modules account for nearly all of the group's runtime.

## Test Plan

Full `tests/kernels/attention` run before and after the change, on a single MI300, same flags and same GPU in both cases. The result was then confirmed a second time with a default environment, to rule out any influence of the flags used while measuring. `test_merge_attn_states.py` was additionally measured on its own, and the unlocked cases were verified independently against the Triton reference path.

## Test Result

Whole group, single MI300:

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Wall time | 46:34 | 10:08 |
| Passed | 3207 | 5808 |
| Skipped | 3703 | 1111 |
| Failed | 0 | 0 |

The group is 4.6x faster while running 2601 more tests, with no failures.

`test_merge_attn_states.py` alone goes from 7:23 (6 passed, 2592 skipped) to 0:30 with all 2598 cases passing, fp8 variants included.

All numbers above are from a local MI300. A speedup is expected in CI as well, since the removed per-test cost is not hardware specific, but the magnitude there is not measured here.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][DP] Don't assume the engines started when forwarding a wake
commits.pr_body:
Fixes the first of the two problems described in #51476.

## Purpose

`DPCoordinator` holds `engines_running`. Front-ends read it through `dp_engines_running()`, and `wait_for_requests_to_drain()` polls it. It is written in two places, and the two writes are not the same kind of claim:

- **True** is set when the coordinator *forwards* a wake — `FIRST_REQ` → broadcast `START_DP_WAVE` ([coordinator.py:361](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/v1/engine/coordinator.py#L361)). Nothing is confirmed; the coordinator assumes the engines will act on the broadcast.
- **False** is set when DP rank 0 reports `wave_complete`, having observed the group go idle.

True is a prediction. False is an observation.

The two-phase pause added `ignore_start_dp_wave`: once the ranks reach pause consensus, **every rank discards `START_DP_WAVE`** ([core.py:2054](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/v1/engine/core.py#L2054)). That removes the premise the prediction rests on. A request arriving after `pause_generation(mode="abort")` makes the coordinator set True, no engine steps, no `wave_complete` is ever produced, and the flag stays True for the life of the process.

The state is unrecoverable: aborting the request does not help, because nothing makes a paused engine step. `wait_for_requests_to_drain()` can then only end in a `TimeoutError`, and the stale True is published to every front-end, where `add_request_async` skips `FIRST_REQ` because it believes the engines are already running.

This is not pause-specific: any mechanism that stops engines from stepping reaches the same state. A request arriving while the engines are `sleep()`ing latches the flag identically, which the second of the two new tests pins down. `_drain_requests_for_elastic_ep` is the only in-tree caller of `wait_for_requests_to_drain`, so that scaling path takes its go/no-go from the same signal.

## Change

Stop predicting. Report both edges from where they happen.

- `coordinator.py`: the `FIRST_REQ` branch still broadcasts, but no longer claims the result.
- `core.py`: rank 0 already reports the True→False edge as `wave_complete`. It now reports False→True from the same place, as the `elif` of that branch, reusing the existing `start_wave` field that the coordinator already interprets as "engines started" ([coordinator.py:436](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/v1/engine/coordinator.py#L436)).

The report sits after `self.engines_running = self._has_global_unfinished_reqs(...)`, which is where the engine that received the request actually transitions — an equal-wave `ADD` does not set the flag in `add_request`. Reporting from the top of the busy loop instead reads the previous iteration's value and misses the edge entirely; the first assertion in the pause test exists to catch exactly that.

Three guards on the new branch: `not was_running` makes it an edge rather than a per-iteration message; `dp_rank == 0` keeps a single writer, matching the existing `wave_complete` convention; `not pending_pause` excludes the kick-start in phase 1 of the pause protocol, which sets `engines_running = True` only so that an idle rank stops `continue`-ing and reaches the consensus all-reduce.

No new message type, no new field, no new socket, and no notion of pausing inside the coordinator. Its `engines_running` becomes rank 0's `engines_running`, one message behind: a single writer, both edges from one source.

### Not #38009

[#38009](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/38009) was rejected for adding per-engine state that diverged across ranks and deadlocked an all-reduce. Here the decision stays in the single coordinator process. The engine side gains one `output_queue.put_nowait` — a report, not a decision — emitted by rank 0 only, after the existing collective has completed. `was_running` is a per-iteration local snapshot: it does not change any rank's participation in any collective, nor any input to `sync_dp_state()`.

### Cost

The coordinator now lags engine start by one round trip (broadcast → step → report). Walking every reader of the flag:

| path | which copy it reads | effect |
|---|---|---|
| offline `LLMEngine` (`SyncMPClient`) | its own local copy — `add_request` sets True, `wave_complete` sets False | none; coordinator publishes never reach it |
| SPMD / no coordinator | — | none; the new report is gated on `has_coordinator` |
| elastic-EP state sync (`elastic_state.py`) | the engine's own `engines_running` | none |
| online API server (`DPAsyncMPClient`) | the coordinator's 100ms publish | a second `FIRST_REQ` can be sent inside the lag window, costing one extra broadcast; engines are idempotent there, so it never causes an extra step |
| `wait_for_requests_to_drain` | same | can return one round trip early |

Measured on 2-way DP + EP with the coordinator instrumented, over four wave starts: **4 `START_DP_WAVE` broadcasts unpatched, 7 patched**, with rank 0 emitting exactly one `start_wave` report per wave start. The extra broadcast is the coordinator's own echo when it processes the report. A burst of 16 concurrent requests produced **one** broadcast in both arms — the client-side `FIRST_REQ` throttle is untouched.

The early return trades a false positive that hangs for 300s and cannot recover for a false negative of a few milliseconds, and downstream operations carry their own barrier (`sleep()` contains the pause consensus). That window is not removable in this architecture: an engine that is not stepping cannot report, so any scheme that waits for an acknowledgement re-latches under pause.

## Test Plan

Two tests in `tests/v1/distributed/test_async_llm_dp.py`, MoE-only because `enable_wave_coordination` is `model_config.is_moe`, so a dense model never reaches this coordinator state.

`test_dp_pause_late_request_does_not_block_drain` has to rule out two different failures, since a signal that is never True satisfies every drain assertion while being useless. It asserts, in order:

1. the engines report themselves as running two seconds into a live request — past the coordinator's 100ms publishes, so the front-end's own optimistic value has been overwritten by then;
2. the flag returns to False when that request finishes;
3. after `pause(mode="abort")` and a late request, the flag first goes True (the latch is armed — otherwise the next assertion is vacuous) and then settles back to False by itself;
4. the late request was held rather than dropped, and completes on resume.

`test_dp_sleep_late_request_does_not_block_drain` pins the same latch reached through `sleep()`, with the same arm-then-settle structure, and checks the held request survives `wake_up()`. It is worth guarding separately because it is the shape that reaches `_drain_requests_for_elastic_ep`.

## Test Result

All runs on `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly` (`0.26.1rc1.dev457+gc810e5ee9`) with this diff applied to the image's `site-packages`, each arm printing which variant it loaded. `before` is the unpatched image; `after` is the same image with this change.

| suite | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `test_async_llm_dp.py -k "dp_pause or dp_sleep"` | **2 failed** / 8 passed | **10 passed** |
| `test_engine_core_client.py` (4 GPUs, full file) | 22 passed | 22 passed |
| `test_pp_dp_v2.py` (DP=2, PP=2, MoE) | 6 passed | 6 passed |
| `test_internal_lb_dp.py` (1 and 4 API servers) | 10 passed | 10 passed |

The two `before` failures are exactly the two new tests, each failing on the assertion that the flag settles back to False. Every pre-existing case passes in both arms, including `test_dp_pause_keep_race_staggered_engines` and `test_dp_pause_barrier_request_deadlock`, the all-reduce rendezvous guards. The full `test_async_llm_dp.py` file, with ray installed, is 23 passed / 4 skipped in the `after` arm.

Beyond the suites, on 2-way DP + EP:

- **Scenarios.** A live request must report True; it must return to False when idle; a late request after `pause(abort)` must settle back; a request admitted microseconds before the pause lands must not strand drain; a request arriving while `sleep()`ing must not latch and must complete on `wake_up()`. All pass. The pause and sleep cases latch on unpatched code — polling for 30s after the late request never observes False, in either flavour. The instrumented coordinator log shows every True paired with a later `wave_complete`, and no True at all while paused or asleep.
- **Stress.** 20 rounds alternating `abort`/`keep`/`wait`, varying in-flight request count and how long before the pause lands: 0 hangs, every request completed, identical to baseline.

## Essential Elements

- Not a duplicate: no open PR matches `engines_running`, `DPCoordinator drain`, or `pause coordinator`. Filed as part of #51476.
- Control-plane only; no effect on model output, so no eval run is included.
- AI assistance was used. The submitter has reviewed each changed line and the runs above.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Detect all attention-spelling variants in ModelConfig.is_hybrid
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

  `ModelConfig.is_hybrid`'s carve-out for granite-4.0-micro (a hybrid-capable architecture with zero actual mamba layers) only matched `layer_types` entries spelled `"attention"`. Transformers >= 5.13 normalizes pure-attention entries to `"full_attention"` instead (the model's own
  `granitemoehybrid.py` already handles both spellings in `ALL_DECODER_LAYER_TYPES` for layer dispatch, but `is_hybrid` never learned the new spelling).

  As a result `is_hybrid` stayed `True` for granite-4.0-micro. Combined with prefix caching now defaulting `mamba_cache_mode` to `"align"` for any hybrid-flagged model, `_get_mamba_bufs()` runs unconditionally and hits `AssertionError: no mamba layers in the model` on the first
  inference request — the engine starts and loads fine, then dies on the first completion.

  Fix: match both spellings in the carve-out.

  AI assistance was used to root-cause and author this fix; I reviewed every changed line and reproduced/verified the behavior end-to-end myself before opening this PR.

  ## Test Plan

  Reproduced on vLLM HEAD `37c3bdf5a` (2026-08-13):
```
  vllm serve ibm-granite/granite-4.0-micro --max-model-len 8192
  # then, once the server is up:
  curl http://localhost:8000/v1/completions \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d '{"model":"ibm-granite/granite-4.0-micro","prompt":"The capital of France is","max_tokens":10}'
```

  Then applied the fix and repeated the same two steps, plus a direct property check:
```python
  from vllm.config import ModelConfig
  mc = ModelConfig(model="ibm-granite/granite-4.0-micro")
  print(mc.is_hybrid)
```

  ## Test Result

  **Before fix:** server starts and loads the model successfully, then the completion request fails the engine:
```
  AssertionError: no mamba layers in the model
    File ".../vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py", line 4437, in execute_model
      mamba_bufs = self._get_mamba_bufs()
    File ".../vllm/v1/worker/mamba_utils.py", line 554, in get_mamba_groups
      assert len(mamba_group_ids) > 0, "no mamba layers in the model"
  vllm.v1.engine.exceptions.EngineDeadError: EngineCore encountered an issue.
```
  `ModelConfig("ibm-granite/granite-4.0-micro").is_hybrid` → `True` (incorrect).

  **After fix:** `is_hybrid` → `False` (correct — this model has no mamba layers). Server starts and the same completion request succeeds:
```json
  {"id":"cmpl-...","choices":[{"text":" Paris.\n\n**Output:**\n..."}], ...}
```
  No crash, no assertion.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][MLA] Do not use Dense MHA for GLM-5.2
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Fix incorrect short-prefill dispatch in the NVIDIA DeepSeek-V3.2 attention
wrapper.

The generic sparse-MLA metadata path may select dense MHA when a prefill's
sequence length is at most `index_topk`. It then allows the sparse indexer to
skip top-k scoring. `DeepseekV32Attention`, however, only invokes
`forward_mqa`; it does not execute the dense-MHA backend. For a pure prefill
above the backend's decode-like threshold, MQA therefore consumed the cleared
all-`-1` top-k buffer and GLM-5.2 output degenerated into repeated tokens.

This change adds a model-layer dense-prefill capability in addition to the
backend capability. The NVIDIA DeepSeek-V3.2 wrapper declares that it is
MQA-only, so sparse MLA keeps its prefill on top-k MQA and the indexer does not
advertise the dense-MHA scoring skip.

This does not duplicate the open related work:

- #51395 disables dense prefill only for the SM120 sparse-MLA backend.
- #52046 adds a dense branch for the PCP path; the reproduced failure is the
  non-PCP SM100 path.
- #49790 routes DSA architectures to the NVIDIA implementation but does not
  resolve this dispatch mismatch.

Issue #46715 reports a different GLM-5.1 failure at a 65,536-token scheduler
budget and multi-thousand-token prompts on the registered model path.

## Test Plan

```text
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/model_executor/layers/test_mla_short_prefill_indexer.py -q

pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/model_executor/layers/attention/mla_attention.py \
  vllm/models/deepseek_v32/attention.py \
  tests/model_executor/layers/test_mla_short_prefill_indexer.py
```

Real-model validation uses `nvidia/GLM-5.2-NVFP4`, TP=4, the explicit NVIDIA
DeepSeek-V3.2 class override, FP8 E4M3 KV cache, eager execution, FP32 indexer
logits, GVR disabled, and FlashInfer autotuning disabled. It serially probes
the 128/129-token routing boundary without setting
`sparse_mla_force_mqa=true`.

## Test Result

- Focused pytest: `7 passed`.
- Pre-commit on all three changed files: all hooks passed.
- `compileall` and `git diff --check`: passed.
- Before this change, the real model passed through 127 actual prompt tokens
  and failed at 129 and every tested larger prompt through 1,001 tokens. Adding
  only `sparse_mla_force_mqa=true` made all 19 boundary cases pass, causally
  confirming the routing mismatch.
- Patched real-model result: all 19/19 cases passed exact retrieval without the
  force-MQA workaround, spanning 97, 101, 122, 127, 129, 130, 131, 132, 162,
  191, 192, 193, 194, 196, 202, 257, 301, 502, and 1,001 actual prompt tokens.

AI assistance was used to diagnose, implement, test, and draft this change.
The human submitter must review every changed line and understand and defend
the change end-to-end before marking the PR ready for review.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Perf] Enable fused KDA decode on gfx942 (MI325X)
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

PR #50654 added the fused Kimi-K3 KDA decode kernel (`csrc/libtorch_stable/kimi_k3/fused_kda_decode_kernel_rocm.cu`), but gated it to gfx950 (MI355X) in two places, so it never activates on gfx942 (MI325X):

- **Build gate** — `CMakeLists.txt` filtered the HIP source to `gfx950` only, so the kernel was not compiled and `VLLM_ENABLE_FUSED_KDA_DECODE` (and therefore `torch.ops._C.fused_kda_decode`) was never defined on a gfx942-only build.
- **Runtime gate** — `is_fused_kda_decode_supported()` in `vllm/models/kimi_k3/amd/ops/kda_decode.py` ended with `return on_gfx950()`.

This change extends both gates to gfx942 as well, so MI325X can take the fused decode path instead of falling back to the three-launch Triton path.

The kernel body is unchanged. It uses only CDNA-common primitives — wave64, DPP row/quad permutes (`quad_perm`, `row_half_mirror`, `row_mirror`), `__builtin_nontemporal_load/store`, and bf16 intrinsics — with no MFMA / FP8 / gfx950-only paths, so no source-level changes are required for gfx942. LDS use is ~2.8 KiB/block and register pressure ~130 VGPR, both well within CDNA3 limits.

## Changes

- `CMakeLists.txt`: HIP arch filter `gfx950` -> `gfx942|gfx950` (and comment).
- `vllm/models/kimi_k3/amd/ops/kda_decode.py`: gate `on_gfx950()` -> `on_gfx950() or on_gfx942()`.
- `tests/models/kimi_k3/test_amd_kda_decode.py`: extend the module skip guard from gfx950 to gfx942 / gfx950 so the correctness suite runs on MI325X.

All other backends and the CUDA path are unchanged; the shape/dtype/head-count guards in `is_fused_kda_decode_supported()` are unchanged.

## Performance

The kernel-level win is large, but the end-to-end win on MI325X is currently small: the Kimi-K3 decode step is dominated by the MXFP4 MoE (int4) and the MLA attention plus the TP8 collectives, which dwarf the KDA linear-attention block. The fusion removes ~66 us of per-layer kernel time (mostly launch overhead), but that is a small fraction of today's total per-token cost. It should become more visible once #50817 (MXFP4 MoE Triton a16w4 for gfx942) lands and shrinks the dominant MoE cost — the fixed KDA saving then represents a larger share of a smaller decode step.

### End-to-end (tp8, 256-in / 256-out, max-concurrency 4)

| Metric | Triton fallback | Fused KDA | Delta |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Mean TPOT (ms) | 425.95 | 422.66 | -0.77% |
| P99 TPOT (ms) | 427.64 | 424.19 | -0.81% |
| Output tok/s | 9.29 | 9.36 | +0.75% |
| Mean TTFT (ms) | 1577.24 | 1574.03 | -0.20% (flat) |

TTFT is unchanged, as expected for a decode-only kernel.

### Per-layer kernel sequence (torch profiler medians, us)

Baseline runs the KDA decode as ~16 separate kernels per layer — the conv1d update, the recurrent delta-rule step, and the gated output RMSNorm decomposed into a chain of launch-overhead-bound (~4 us floor) elementwise ops. Fused collapses all of them into a single kernel:

| # | Baseline kernel | us | Fused kernel | us |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | _causal_conv1d_update_kernel | 5.01 | kda_decode_fusion_kernel<true, 12, true, true, true> | 7.77 |
| 2 | fused_recurrent_kda_packed_decode_kernel | 6.45 | | |
| 3 | __amd_rocclr_copyBuffer | 4.37 | | |
| 4 | bfloat16->float32 copy | 4.41 | | |
| 5 | pow (tensor, scalar) | 4.41 | | |
| 6 | reduce Mean | 5.01 | | |
| 7 | add | 4.45 | | |
| 8 | rsqrt | 4.37 | | |
| 9 | mul | 4.21 | | |
| 10 | bfloat16->float32 copy | 4.17 | | |
| 11 | mul | 4.21 | | |
| 12 | bfloat16->float32 copy | 4.45 | | |
| 13 | sigmoid | 5.05 | | |
| 14 | mul | 4.33 | | |
| 15 | float32->bfloat16 copy | 4.49 | | |
| 16 | __amd_rocclr_copyBuffer | 4.57 | | |
| | **total (16 kernels)** | **~73.96** | **total (1 kernel)** | **7.77** |

~9.5x less kernel time for the KDA decode block (~74 -> 7.8 us/layer). The `12` template arg is 12 heads/rank (96 KDA heads at TP8). Across the model's KDA layers (~69 per the kernel header) that is ~4.6 ms/token of raw kernel time removed, in the same ballpark as the ~3.3 ms/token TPOT drop measured above (the remainder overlaps with other work).

## Not a duplicate


- `gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "KDA decode gfx942"`
- `gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "fused_kda_decode MI325"`

## Test Plan

Run on an MI325X (gfx942) box after building with gfx942 in the arch list:

1. Build compiles the kernel and registers the op: `python -c "import torch, vllm; print(hasattr(torch.ops._C, 'fused_kda_decode'))"` -> expect `True`.
2. Kernel correctness: `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/kimi_k3/test_amd_kda_decode.py -v`
3. Model accuracy (output-affecting change) — serve Kimi-K3 on MI325X and run gsm8k, compared against the Triton fallback path: `make gsm8k`
4. Decode latency / throughput before vs after (fused vs Triton fallback): `make bench-kda-mi325`

## Test Result


- Op registered: **True** on the gfx942 build (`hasattr(torch.ops._C, "fused_kda_decode")`); the fused kernel appears in the trace (see Performance).
- Latency/throughput: **-0.77% mean TPOT**, +0.75% output tok/s
- gsm8k (fused vs Triton): **parity** — both 1.00 exact_match on flexible-extract and strict-match (5-shot, limit=100, stderr 0). The fused kernel matches the Triton fallback exactly.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm] Gate Torch FP8 scaled-MM on architecture support
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Reject Torch FP8 scaled-MM kernels when the underlying PyTorch operator is unavailable.

The existing implementation compares a CUDA-style numeric capability against the SM89 threshold. On ROCm, gfx1100 reports capability `110`, so it incorrectly passes this check even though RDNA3 has no native FP8 matrix support and `torch._scaled_mm` rejects the device at runtime.

This change mirrors PyTorch’s current ROCm architecture gate for per-tensor, channel-wise, and row-wise Torch FP8 kernels while preserving existing CPU, CUDA, and XPU behavior. It does not change general FP8 support for Triton, upcast, or emulation paths.

This does not duplicate #43615: that PR enables RDNA4 paths but does not fix the inherited per-tensor/channel-wise eligibility check on gfx1100.

Once `torch.cuda.is_scaled_mm_supported()` is available in vLLM’s supported PyTorch baseline, the mirrored architecture gate can be replaced with that query.

AI assistance was used; all changed lines were reviewed by the submitter.

## Test Plan

```bash
ruff check vllm/model_executor/kernels/linear/scaled_mm/pytorch.py
ruff format --check vllm/model_executor/kernels/linear/scaled_mm/pytorch.py
git diff --check

HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 python /tmp/validate_vllm_fp8_scaled_mm.py
HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1 python /tmp/validate_vllm_fp8_scaled_mm.py
```

The standalone script validates:

- CPU, XPU, CUDA, and ROCm routing behavior.
- gfx1100 rejects all three Torch FP8 scaled-MM variants.
- gfx1201 accepts all three variants.
- The underlying PyTorch operator rejects gfx1100.
- Tensor-wise and row-wise execution succeeds on gfx1201 and matches an FP32 reference.

## Test Result

- Ruff passed.
- Formatting passed.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- Platform-routing matrix passed:
  - CPU/XPU supported.
  - CUDA FP8 capability preserved.
  - Unsupported ROCm rejected.
  - Supported ROCm accepted.

gfx1100:

```text
selected=[False, False, False], operator=rejected
```

gfx1201:

```text
selected=[True, True, True], tensorwise=ok, rowwise=ok,
relative_error=0.001601
```

The local vLLM extensions were ABI-incompatible with the installed PyTorch, so validation covered vLLM’s Python selection logic and the underlying PyTorch operator directly rather than a full end-to-end model serving run.

commits.pr_title: Remove VLLM_TEST_FORCE_FP8_MARLIN to replace with linear_backend/moe_backend
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Remove the test-only `VLLM_TEST_FORCE_FP8_MARLIN` environment variable and use the public `linear_backend` / `moe_backend` configuration to force Marlin. Marlin remains available as the FP8 fallback when earlier compatible kernels cannot be selected.

This also fixes the CI failures exposed by that fallback path:

- use realistic 128 x 128 block-FP8 test shapes instead of synthetic 1 x 1 blocks;
- give `TestFP8Layer` the partition metadata and device placement expected by real FP8 layers;
- skip forced-kernel fusion assertions when the requested kernel is unsupported and selection correctly falls back to a different kernel.

The root cause was not that Marlin was selected incorrectly. On the failing L4 cases, the explicitly requested FlashInfer, DeepGEMM, or CUTLASS kernel was unsupported, so selection continued to Marlin. The fixtures then either lacked the metadata Marlin needs or asserted fusion behavior belonging to the unavailable requested kernel.

This is not a duplicate contribution: it updates the existing PR that introduced/exposed these CI failures; no separate PR implements this fix.

commits.pr_title: [MOE] Standardize and abstract fused shared expert optimization selection
commits.pr_body:
## Disclosure

AI assistance was used. The changes were reviewed and tested manually.

## Purpose

Standardize fused shared-expert (FSE) detection so model construction and checkpoint loading use the same quantization-compatible decision **throughout all models implementing FSE**.

This is e.g. useful for:

- `shared_expert` fusion through arbitrary quantization methods/config (e.g. later on with online quantization in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51285 / https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51392), so that FSE compatibility can be detected more largely based on arbitrary quantization config across all model archs, and not simply based on logic specific to e.g. [qwen3/quark](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/fac808b36f502d0d992509a187dca94c68b0360a/vllm/model_executor/models/qwen3_next.py#L81-L98 )
- Be less bug-prone where FSE resolution is done differently in many different places
- Make FSE API less dependent on ROCm/AITER, so that it will be useful e.g. as well for https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/50963 that is NOT rocm/aiter specific.

The shared resolver validates FSE against the quantization configuration, rejects an incompatible requested FSE configuration, and ensures all MoE layers in a model agree on the resolved state. The mixed-state error reports the counts of enabled and disabled layers.

Behavior change compared with `main`:

- Models with mixed resolved FSE states now raise `NotImplementedError`. FSE is only supported/tested for all (or none) layers currently, within a PP rank.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][PaliGemma] Remove stale image embedding scaling
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Fixes #52667.

After Gemma moved the `sqrt(hidden_size)` scaling into text embedding lookup, PaliGemma continued to apply the old `hidden_size**-0.5` factor to projected image features. This left image embeddings at approximately `1 / sqrt(hidden_size)` of the expected magnitude. Remove the stale image-side scaling so PaliGemma passes raw projected image features to the Gemma input embedding merge, matching the Transformers contract.

This is a focused bug fix: it changes no vision projection, tokenizer, scheduler, or kernel behavior.
